basis: Defined by developmental impairment, epilepsy, movement disorders and other neurological dysfunction.
Complete developmental absence of teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Renal dysgenesis, thymic aplasia and lung dysplasia define the syndrome; anal atresia is a defining gastrointestinal malformation.
Broad deletion umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment or peripheral neuropathy predominates across major subgroups. Other organ defects depend on the deleted interval.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; persistent vocal cord paresis affects 8/8 and structural foot deformity (pes cavus) affects 6/8.
Eversion of the eyelid margin exposes the conjunctiva; confined to the ocular adnexa.
Infection of orbital bone, involving both skeletal tissue and the orbital eye adnexa.
Malignant neoplasm of skull bone; additional sites represented by individual subtypes do not characterize the umbrella.
Congenital structural defects of the anus and distal rectum, including stenosis and fistulas.
Autoimmune CNS demyelination; optic nerve demyelination causes visual dysfunction in roughly half over the course of multiple sclerosis, the listed subtype.
Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; developmental impairment/polyneuropathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and muscle weakness with COX-negative fibers occur in the sole reported patient.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, present in 3/3 annotated patients.
Benign capillary neoplasm arising in the breast; breast is outside the organ axes.
Immune-mediated microscopic inflammation and collagen deposition in colonic mucosa cause chronic watery diarrhea.
Disease of the ulnar peripheral nerve causing motor and sensory deficits.
Adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma with fibrous stroma, usually retroperitoneal or paratesticular; no consistent visceral organ involvement.
Skin/oral hamartomas and polyposis define disease; goiter 80-99%, neurodevelopmental impairment 30-79% in HPO. Cancer risks excluded; conjunctival hamartomas lack demonstrated impairment.
Cleft lip/palate, congenital heart defects and hearing loss define syndrome; high myopia occurs in 6/7, with additional destructive ocular lesions reported.
Ehrlichia infects leukocytes and commonly causes leukopenia and thrombocytopenia. Transient liver enzyme elevations alone do not establish lasting hepatic damage.
Inherited epidermal fragility with recurrent intraepidermal vesicles and blisters; no autoimmune mechanism.
Congenital absence or hypoplasia of fifth-digit bones in all four limbs; manifestations are isolated to the skeleton.
Congenital deafness and temporal hypotrichosis; tongue/palate malformations occur in 80-99%, dental abnormalities and patent ductus arteriosus in 30-79% per HPO.
ATP synthase metabolic deficiency; neurological regression affects 4/4 and ophthalmoplegia 2/4. Cardiomyopathy in 1/4 falls below the threshold.
Lymphoid malignancy centered in the tonsil of the oropharynx; pharyngeal structures belong to the pulmonary axis.
Abnormal collagen synthesis in lamellar bone causes skeletal fragility and spontaneous fractures; manifestations are explicitly limited to the skeleton.
